completionRule: No unresolved Critical or High finding may omit a backlog owner and workstream. Fixed contracts may retain owned production-integration work.

findings.title: Project schemas, runtime validator, and examples described incompatible v3 semantics
findings.failureScenario: A swarm can produce a file that passes one schema or example but is rejected by the runtime, or silently omit compatibility fields that control execution.
findings.repair: Establish project v3 as the sole new-write authority, add strict compatibility versions and unknown-field checks, align JSON Schema/examples, and validate every fixture against both schema and runtime.
regressionTests: FR-01 project v3 validation and semantic digest
Draft 2020-12 schema validation of v3 example

findings.title: Legacy migration represented semantic loss as a clean upgrade
findings.failureScenario: A v1/v2 project opens as v3 while operator meaning, track membership, or lab state cannot be reconstructed; agents then execute a plausible but different composition.
findings.repair: Emit migration receipt v2 with source/target digests, preserved opaque extensions, blocking loss records, and requiresUserReview; quarantine catalog rebinding.

findings.title: Command JSON schema and TypeScript envelope used incompatible grammars and trusted UI inverse data
findings.failureScenario: A command serialized by one agent cannot be replayed by another; worse, a stale or malicious UI can provide an inverse that corrupts Undo.
findings.repair: Replace with command v2: one PascalCase grammar, typed target/write sets, preconditions, clone-first atomic transactions, core-generated validated inverses, no-op suppression, and explicit history semantics.

findings.title: Persistent IDs and random streams were collision-prone and evaluation-order dependent
findings.failureScenario: Different tuples can share the same legacy serialized input/hash; adding a draw in one branch changes sibling generated output and invalidates stable selections, exceptions, or project replay.
findings.repair: Introduce typed canonical value encoding, SHA-256 digests, bounded stable-ID v2, and immutable named PRNG streams derived from root seed plus path. Keep v1 migration-only.

findings.title: Audio plan mixed immutable musical content with runtime generation/transport state and quantized duration incorrectly
findings.failureScenario: The same plan hashes differently per playback, offline and realtime disagree, and a short event can become zero or gain a frame because duration is rounded separately instead of quantizing absolute endpoints.
findings.repair: Define immutable ResolvedAudioPlan v2 in project-timeline seconds, separate AudioScheduleBinding v1 for generation/transport/backend epoch, and quantize absolute start/end once.
findings.contractVersionChange: resolved audio plan 1→2; schedule binding new v1

findings.title: Cancellation was capable of being mistaken for async freshness
findings.failureScenario: A canceled worker finishes late and publishes stale geometry, provenance, materialization, or audio plan because cancellation state—not current semantic identity—is treated as proof.
findings.repair: Use project epoch, scope, channel, generation, input/environment/catalog/budget hashes, payload integrity, and current desired identity; cancellation is resource control only.

findings.title: Package manifest trusted declared paths, sizes, and hashes without verifying actual archive members
findings.failureScenario: A hostile archive uses traversal, links, case collisions, compression bombs, undeclared files, or false sizes/hashes to overwrite files or bypass semantic validation.
findings.repair: Define package manifest v2, strict portable paths, content-addressed assets, measured member metadata, no links/devices, no extra/missing members, bounded totals/ratios, and validated authoritative project.

findings.title: Exact rational construction accepted unsafe or approximate Number input
findings.failureScenario: An integer beyond 2^53 or decimal parsed through binary floating point silently changes a beat, range, seed input, or cache key.
findings.repair: Require exact string/scientific/fraction parsing, canonical rational wire validation, and an explicitly named approximate-number conversion seam.

findings.title: Tempo curve meaning and beat/seconds conversion were underdefined
findings.failureScenario: Web and native agents implement different linear-tempo interpolation or repeatedly add floating deltas, causing drift and cross-platform event disagreement.
findings.repair: Version tempo-map v1; keep beats exact, define step and linear-BPM-over-beat analytic integration/inversion, and emit deterministic seconds only at the render boundary.

findings.title: Operator definitions and catalogs could mutate after registration
findings.failureScenario: One agent modifies a shared definition object after another computed a project or graph digest; the same type/version then means different behavior.
findings.repair: Deep-clone/freeze definitions, validate parameters including explicit null, compute versioned semantic digests, seal catalogs, and persist catalog/operator digests.

findings.title: No single graph compiler enforced types, cardinality, cycles, and operator digests
findings.failureScenario: The UI accepts a wire that the evaluator rejects, or different agents compute dependency closure/order differently, creating invalid saved graphs and divergent sound.
findings.repair: Compile through one deterministic service that verifies catalog digest, node parameters, ports/types/dimensions/cardinality/required inputs, result cycles, topological order, and dependency closure.

findings.title: Transaction application could partially mutate caller state before failure
findings.failureScenario: Command 2 of 3 fails after command 1 mutates a shared object, leaving project state changed without a committed transaction or inverse.
findings.repair: Clone before apply, validate all transaction envelope invariants, compute/validate inverse per command, and only publish the final clone after all commands succeed.

findings.title: Time-only command coalescing could merge distinct user intents
findings.failureScenario: Two edits close in time become one Undo step, or one gesture becomes many steps across platforms.
findings.repair: Coalesce only one explicit edit session with identical action, target set, and write set; preserve first-before/final-after; no time-only merge.

findings.title: Looped pattern evaluation could exceed budgets before checking and omit long events crossing the query boundary
findings.failureScenario: A recursive/looping clip allocates millions of events before failure, while long notes begun in a prior cycle disappear from playback or export.
findings.repair: Preflight conservative event counts, include prior cycles needed for overlapping durations, enforce half-open interval semantics, stable ordering, and bounded IDs.

findings.title: Material source status conflated unknown evidence with missing source
findings.failureScenario: A snapshot whose current digest is not yet evaluated is shown as missing or changed, prompting destructive rematerialization or false provenance claims.
findings.repair: Add unresolved state; derive status from material kind, source existence/detachment, and exact dependency digest rather than persist it as truth.

findings.title: Materialization could commit output prepared from an obsolete source
findings.failureScenario: The generator changes while freeze runs; completion writes a snapshot different from what the user saw/requested.
findings.repair: Use prepare-then-commit with exact half-open range, project epoch, dependency/recipe/environment/catalog/artifact hashes, ID collision checks, and atomic commit failure on drift.

findings.title: Selection identity included projection path or generated display ID
findings.failureScenario: Selecting one mathematical entity in timeline and canvas produces two selections, or regenerated display IDs orphan/rebind the wrong entity.
findings.repair: Define semantic selection v2 independent of projection and generated display/fingerprint; projection keys are separate; orphan reactivation requires exact key and unchanged intent epoch.

findings.title: Export could silently flatten procedural or geometric meaning
findings.failureScenario: MIDI or MusicXML appears to preserve a live generator/Penrose structure when it only contains a bounded note realization; later audit cannot identify source recipes, receipts, range, plan, or losses.
findings.repair: Require immutable source/project/environment/catalog/plan bindings, mode-consistent recipes/receipts, output hash, provenance, exact range, canonical media type, and explicit procedural/MusicXML loss records.

findings.title: Accessibility semantics were at risk of becoming separate per-surface approximations
findings.failureScenario: Canvas supports only drag/color/motion, keyboard focus forms cycles or follows expensive selection, and web/native announce different states.
findings.repair: Use one acyclic semantic mirror with stable order/roles/state text/actions, exact value controls, non-drag alternatives, one focus locus, and shared projection data.

findings.title: Research-gated claim authorization trusted caller-supplied evidence IDs
findings.failureScenario: UI code passes an arbitrary evidence string and publishes “exact Penrose” or “validated Risset” before the required implementation/study exists.
findings.repair: Bind claims to allowed surfaces, exact qualification digest, sources, and trusted release-context gate evidence; caller strings cannot satisfy gates.

findings.title: Risset event ordinals could exceed safe integer identity space
findings.failureScenario: Very long/high-rate queries round event ordinals, collide IDs, loop indefinitely, or generate nonfinite inverse times.
findings.repair: Preflight bounded horizon/event count, require safe layer/ordinal indices and finite phase/rate/inverse time, and fail deterministically before enumeration.
regressionTests: FR-01 Risset bounded closure/unsafe ordinal test

findings.title: Penrose canonical identity and topology could depend on unbounded text or Float64 projection
findings.failureScenario: Huge exact addresses create giant persisted IDs/DoS, or two vertices/edges merge because their rendered coordinates fall within an epsilon.
findings.repair: Validate family/address ranges and canonical tuples, use bounded SHA-256 IDs over exact addresses, keep Q(phi) topology exact, and reject nonfinite Float64 projection.

findings.title: Public JSON schemas and runtime validators could drift independently
findings.failureScenario: A fixture passes Draft 2020-12 schema but fails runtime—or vice versa—so autonomous agents choose different authorities.
findings.repair: Align versioned schemas/fixtures and run all public examples/fixtures through JSON Schema plus runtime validators in check:all; fail missing/mismatched artifacts.

findings.title: Swift contracts lagged project v3, semantic selection, source status, stable IDs, and PRNG
findings.failureScenario: The iPad opens the file but assigns different generated identities/random output or treats the same canvas/timeline entity as different selections.
findings.repair: Add project v3 DTOs, unresolved source status, package profile v2, semantic selection v2, pure SHA-256/canonical stable-ID v2, named PRNG v2, and shared fixtures.

findings.title: Playable prototypes still bypass the production render-plan/backend architecture
findings.failureScenario: The current demo sounds correct while production scheduler/offline/native paths execute different timing, voice, cancellation, or safety semantics.
findings.repair: Migrate Infinite Staircase/Euclidean and all voices to finalized plan v2 plus schedule binding; prohibit lab-local timing authority.

findings.title: Cross-browser scheduler and realtime/offline tolerances are unmeasured
findings.failureScenario: A hard-coded 25/100 ms profile works on one desktop but misses notes, makes edits sluggish, or overloads native nodes elsewhere.
findings.affectedFilesOrContracts: DR-03 benchmark harness; AGL audio diagnostics
findings.repair: Run declared browser/OS/hardware matrix; calibrate horizon, late policy, native/worklet threshold, cancellation, latency telemetry, and feature tolerances.

findings.title: Exact Penrose runtime still lacks recovered golden/oracle/matching artifacts and generator
findings.failureScenario: A visually convincing patch ships without exact matching, adjacency/query completeness, or independent oracle proof.
findings.repair: Recover or regenerate fixture bytes/prototypes/legal stars/matching tables; implement exact pentagrid generator, cut-and-project/hierarchy oracles, halo, clipping, adjacency, and traversal.
regressionTests: future DR-09 goldens and property suite

findings.title: Export manifests exist but WAV/MIDI/MusicXML/package codecs are not production implementations
findings.failureScenario: A swarm treats the manifest contract as evidence that real export is complete, while codec timing, tails, quantization, loss records, and transactional output are untested.
findings.repair: Implement codecs from canonical events/plans, transactional files, tails, loss fixtures, and round-trip tests.
regressionTests: future export corpus and end-to-end smoke

findings.title: Claim registry enforcement is not yet wired to product copy/build
findings.failureScenario: A component bypasses claim resolution and hard-codes an overclaim even though the registry is correct.
findings.repair: Require registered claim IDs for scientific copy, lint generated docs/examples/UI, and make missing qualification/gate fail CI/release review.

findings.title: Profile-numeric behavior remains undefined for chaos and other floating workloads
findings.failureScenario: TypeScript and Swift choose different branch/quantization outcomes from tiny float differences, changing persisted events, IDs, or cache results.
findings.affectedFilesOrContracts: program/backlog AGL-170; chaos/control operators; cache policy
findings.repair: Define exact versus profile-numeric classes, checkpoints, absolute/relative/ULP tolerances, NaN/signed-zero, branch quantization, backend provenance, and cache namespace.

findings.title: Legacy migrated operators require explicit sealed-catalog rebinding
findings.failureScenario: A legacy type/version is assigned a synthetic digest and executed as if it had authoritative historical semantics.
findings.repair: Prevent execution while blocking loss exists; show preserved source, choose compatible catalog definition, record signed rebinding receipt, or keep read-only.

findings.title: Physical package profile and iCloud/File Provider conflict behavior remain unproven
findings.failureScenario: Web archive and native directory package produce different logical files or two offline edits overwrite one another without preserving both versions.
findings.affectedFilesOrContracts: native package adapter; browser archive adapter; DR-12 POA
findings.repair: Prove identical logical member set/digest, single-writer policy, conflict preservation, rename/move/eviction, hostile archive, and rollback.

findings.title: Transport generation cutover and runtime graph failure behavior are contracts without production state machines
findings.failureScenario: A valid document edit compiles late; the UI shows new graph while old audio keeps playing silently, or stale worklet events fire after seek.
findings.affectedFilesOrContracts: transport; audio backend; graph candidate/active plan state
findings.repair: Implement project/transport epochs, last-valid/candidate/armed/active plan states, exact effective frame, failure/mute scope, tail policy, and telemetry.
regressionTests: future model tests and audio cutover tests

findings.title: Real-time callback boundary is not yet mechanically enforced
findings.failureScenario: An agent calls graph evaluation, allocates provenance, logs, parses JSON, or locks from AudioWorklet/native render callback, causing glitches or deadlocks.
findings.affectedFilesOrContracts: AudioWorklet/native audio modules; code ownership rules
findings.repair: Restrict render path to bounded preallocated queue/voice/DSP code, add static dependency checks and stress tests, and keep domain core off real-time thread.
regressionTests: future architecture lint and underrun stress

findings.title: Generated identity capability is not yet proven for every operator/lab
findings.failureScenario: Sparse exceptions or persistent selections target an output whose topology/key changes under parameter edits, then silently affect the wrong event/tile.
findings.repair: Require stable/successor-mapped/ephemeral declaration, key schema/version, metamorphic identity tests, and capability-gated UI actions.

findings.title: Source-byte preservation and canonical semantic digest serve different purposes
findings.failureScenario: Canonicalization destroys original bytes needed for forensic migration receipts, while raw byte hash cannot identify semantic equality.
findings.repair: Persist source bytes/hash separately from normalized project semantic digest; never use one as a substitute for the other.

findings.title: Command field preconditions need a versioned canonical path vocabulary
findings.failureScenario: Free-form string paths change meaning after schema migration, making stale guards or future collaboration unsafe.
findings.repair: Define field/path IDs by command payload schema, migrate versions explicitly, and forbid arbitrary JSON pointer mutation commands.

findings.title: Exact and profile-numeric cache results require separate compatibility rules
findings.failureScenario: A raw floating result from one engine is reused under another backend/profile and changes threshold or event decisions.
findings.repair: Use backend-independent exact keys only for exact/canonical outputs; include numerical profile/backend/build for raw numeric results until canonicalized.

findings.title: MIDI runtime I/O and Standard MIDI File export could be conflated
findings.failureScenario: Web/native live device timestamps, permissions, UMP/MIDI2 resolution, and SMF quantization are handled as one API and silently lose resolution or clock meaning.
findings.affectedFilesOrContracts: AGL-048; AGL-130; native Core MIDI adapter
findings.repair: Keep ephemeral runtime I/O separate from canonical export; preserve UMP resolution natively, map clocks explicitly, and disclose SMF quantization.

findings.title: Pinned toolchain exists but dependency lock and connected install proof remain incomplete
findings.failureScenario: A local agent resolves a different transitive dependency or uses an unreviewed global toolchain, producing nonreproducible output despite passing source tests.
findings.repair: Run connected npm install, commit lockfile/integrity metadata, enforce exact Node/npm/TS/Swift CI images, license/SBOM, and clean-build receipts.

findings.title: Canonical encoding admitted hidden JavaScript state and malformed Unicode ambiguity
findings.failureScenario: Two values that look identical through normal enumeration can carry accessors, symbol keys, non-enumerable properties, sparse/custom arrays, or lone surrogates and therefore hash or execute inconsistently across JavaScript, UTF-8 encoders, and Swift.
findings.repair: Reject unsupported object shapes and hidden state, validate Unicode scalar well-formedness, enforce depth/node/string/collection/encoded-byte limits, and test SHA parity across block boundaries.
regressionTests: FR-01 SHA-256 Node parity across block boundaries
findings.contractVersionChange: canonical-value-v1 behavior clarified and fail-closed without reinterpreting accepted values

findings.title: Authoritative JSON could be interpreted differently because duplicate keys, unsafe integers, or malformed UTF-8 were accepted
findings.failureScenario: One reader accepts the first duplicate key, another the last, and another rejects it; or a large integer/lone surrogate changes during decode, allowing schema, hash, project ID, or package metadata substitution.
findings.affectedFilesOrContracts: src/core/strict-json.ts; src/core/project-package.ts; schemas/*; native import boundary
findings.repair: Introduce strict UTF-8 JSON parsing with duplicate-member, unsafe-integer, malformed-Unicode, trailing-data, depth/node/collection limits before schema/runtime validation; require native parity.
regressionTests: FR-01 strict JSON duplicate key/unsafe integer/malformed UTF-8 corpus

findings.title: Graph compatibility compared only coarse port labels and omitted complete dimension semantics
findings.failureScenario: UI/compiler accepts a connection whose value kind matches but measurement model, unit, circular period, domain categories/bounds, or missing-value policy differs, producing plausible but semantically invalid mappings.
findings.affectedFilesOrContracts: src/core/graph.ts; operator port DimensionSpec; UI compatibility service
findings.repair: Hash and compare complete dimension semantics and make the compiler compatibility service the sole UI/import authority.
findings.contractVersionChange: graph compiler v2 compatibility semantics hardened

findings.title: Worker results could self-declare an exact determinism class and poison exact caches
findings.failureScenario: A compromised, stale, or buggy worker marks profile-numeric/render-only output as exact, causing backend-dependent values to enter backend-independent cache keys and later publish as authoritative.
findings.repair: Make determinism class host-owned from the sealed operator/catalog contract; worker results echo it only for mismatch detection and cannot promote cache semantics.
findings.contractVersionChange: evaluation protocol v2 host authority clarified

findings.title: Custom transaction cloning could retain references to authoritative nested state
findings.failureScenario: A custom clone function returns a shallow copy; a failing handler mutates nested authoritative state before the transaction is rejected, violating atomicity despite clone-first architecture.
findings.repair: Validate deep graph independence between pre-state, clone, and committed result; reject aliasing custom clones.
regressionTests: FR-01 shallow custom clone rejection and authoritative-state preservation

findings.title: Audio plan runtime, schema, and canonicalization limits disagreed
findings.failureScenario: A plan passes JSON Schema but runtime rejects it, or runtime accepts a plan that exhausts canonicalization memory, causing browser/native/offline differential behavior and denial of service.
findings.repair: Align collection ceilings, lower event limits to bounded MVP values, apply audio-specific canonical limits, and validate plan/schema fixtures together.
regressionTests: FR-01 audio-plan schema/runtime collection limit parity
findings.contractVersionChange: resolved audio plan v2 safety limits clarified

findings.title: Canonical digest and resolved plans are whole-value in-memory operations
findings.failureScenario: A legitimate large project or long export stays below per-collection caps but still requires duplicate whole-object canonical bytes and a whole plan in memory, causing OOM or long uninterruptible work.
findings.affectedFilesOrContracts: src/core/canonical.ts; src/core/render-plan.ts; export pipeline; package writer
findings.repair: Define streaming canonical digest equivalence and deterministic plan/export fragmentation with bounded memory, resumable cancellation, stable fragment IDs, and whole-value compatibility fixtures.
regressionTests: future fragmented-vs-whole plan/export equivalence and cancellation tests
findings.contractVersionChange: future streaming canonical/profile and plan-fragment contract

findings.title: Operator semantic metadata digest does not prove evaluator implementation identity
findings.failureScenario: An agent changes executable operator behavior but leaves type, semantic version, metadata, and digest projection unchanged; projects and caches appear compatible while outputs drift.
findings.affectedFilesOrContracts: src/core/operator.ts; src/operators/*; sealed catalog; release evidence
findings.repair: Create implementation-conformance receipts binding evaluator build/source identity to operator type/version/digest and accepted golden/property fixtures; fail release on behavior change without version advance.

findings.title: Export manifest validation did not prove it described the actual artifact bytes
findings.failureScenario: A manifest passes validation while the produced WAV/MIDI/MusicXML/archive has different bytes, media type, or length, allowing accidental or malicious substitution after semantic checks.
findings.repair: Verify actual bytes, byte count, media type, and SHA-256 against the completed manifest before release or download.
findings.contractVersionChange: export manifest v1 completion semantics hardened

findings.title: Accessibility and claim runtime vocabularies could drift from their JSON schemas and registers
findings.failureScenario: Schema accepts a role/surface/claim class that runtime silently handles differently, or release code omits the declared claim vocabulary, creating inaccessible actions or unauthorized copy.
findings.repair: Validate runtime enum vocabularies and top-level register metadata, add a public claim-register schema, and include both contracts in schema/runtime/release verification.
findings.contractVersionChange: new public claim-register-v1 schema; accessibility mirror v1 runtime parity hardened

findings.title: Swift/native project import still relies on ordinary JSONDecoder rather than the strict hostile JSON contract
findings.failureScenario: The browser rejects duplicate keys, malformed Unicode, or unsafe numbers while the native client decodes them differently and opens a semantically different project/package.
findings.repair: Implement or wrap a strict byte-level native JSON/package preflight and run the identical accepted/rejected hostile corpus before native editing or execution.
